tasks.short: Arrange merchandise and issue promotional materials

steps.what: Agree suitable merchandise display placement and promotional materials with customer
Arrange merchandise and sales promotion displays or issue materials to customers

tasks.design: Retain customer agreement and physical display work. Existing {DOCS} promotional guidance may support the worker, but no separate creation of marketing copy is assumed inside this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Placement depends on the customer's premises and physical merchandise.
tasks.enabler_now: No software capability replaces the physical arrangement proposed here.
tasks.still_hard: Space restrictions, unsuitable displays and customer preferences.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising what works in the actual customer location.
tasks.altitude: No change to display and promotional-material duties.

reach.task: Resolve displays that do not fit the customer location
reach.learn: Which promotional requirements can be adapted

evidence.claim: Physical display arrangement and customer agreement remain human work with no claimed saving.

assumptions: Boundary is driver display work and issuing existing materials, excluding campaign creation and customer selling effort.
s1 produces the agreed placement; no structured space or customer-preference feed is assumed.
Approved materials are unchanged upstream inputs from the promotion process.
No new system, transferred capture or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Display types and customer location requirements
research_questions: Is repetitive promotion administration separately measured from physical placement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+70=100. Customer agreement and physical placement retain all time; upkeep is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect vending cash and replenish machines

steps.what: Collect coins from vending machines using the established custody process
Inspect merchandise remove aged items and refill vending machines

tasks.design: Retain physical coin collection, item inspection and replenishment. Existing {OTHER} vending-machine status may inform the visit, but no telemetry-based removal of visits is claimed for the actual service task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash and merchandise still have to be physically handled.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional software change removes that handling in this design.
tasks.still_hard: Damaged goods, unclear dates and cash custody exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing actual product condition and maintaining secure custody.
tasks.altitude: No change to vending service duties.

reach.task: Resolve machine faults that prevent replenishment or cash access

evidence.claim: The design retains physical vending service and does not infer route or service-time savings from telemetry.

assumptions: Boundary is service at the machine, excluding route planning and later cash accounting.
s2 includes inspecting stock levels, dates and condition before replenishment; no free structured aged-stock flag or par level is assumed.
Existing machine status is an optional unchanged reference and earns no saving.
No new system, capture requirement or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Machine types, stock rotation requirements and custody process
research_questions: Is separate repeated service-record entry a measurable burden outside physical servicing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+75=100. Cash collection, inspection, removal and refill retain full time; upkeep is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write customer orders and sales contracts

steps.what: Confirm customer order details and applicable standard sales terms
Write customer orders and standard sales contract drafts according to company guidelines
outputs: draft customer order and sales contract

steps.what: Compare draft with customer agreement and save checked order and contract draft
inputs: draft customer order and sales contract
outputs: checked customer order and contract draft

tasks.design: Configure order and standard-contract templates in {CRM} using approved product, price and clause records. The worker confirms details with the customer, checks the exact generated draft and saves it for the existing approval/signing route; unusual terms go to the sales manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders and contracts repeat customer, line-item and standard-term information.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can assemble controlled fields and clauses deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Customer requests that do not match standard products or approved terms.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising the difference between a standard order and a commitment needing escalation.
tasks.altitude: Less drafting repetition; negotiation and commitment authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Review nonstandard customer terms before commitment
reach.learn: Which deviations require commercial or legal review

evidence.claim: Controlled templates can assemble standard orders and contracts without a model inventing terms; the deployment and saving are unmeasured model assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is writing and checking the worker's order/contract draft, excluding final company authorisation, customer signing and fulfilment.

s1 counts confirmation and capture of customer ID, product/specification, quantity/unit, agreed price, delivery details, applicable term version and any requested deviation; the worker produces checked inputs.
The existing sales administration process supplies approved product/price records and the legal/commercial process supplies approved clause/template versions through unchanged work.
s2 retains field entry, template selection and manual exception handling; no structured customer order is assumed for free.
Test native template configuration first. Missing terms or nonstandard clauses stop standard generation and follow the current manager route.
s3 checks the exact saved draft; changes invalidate approval. No automatic external contract acceptance is introduced.
unknowns: Native templates, standard-order coverage and worker authority
research_questions: Can controlled templates reduce writing time after retaining customer confirmation and full draft comparison?

already_counted.description: Input/template selection and exceptions in s2
Exact draft comparison and save approval in s3

incremental.description: Inspect template mappings and report outdated standard terms
Maintain additional template and approved-clause configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact customer, line items, quantities, prices, delivery details and approved term/template versions in the saved order/contract draft; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+12+20=72; gross 28 minus 1.5 focal upkeep gives net 26.5. High requires repeated standard drafting; low covers nonstandard terms and manual exceptions consuming the benefit. Other-role template upkeep is separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review customer drops and load trucks

steps.what: Review dealer customer or station-drop lists and check required goods
outputs: understood drop requirements and loading sequence

steps.what: Load trucks with required goods in a suitable secured sequence
inputs: understood drop requirements and loading sequence

tasks.design: Keep reading the drop requirements and physically loading the truck with the worker. An existing {OPS_SYSTEM} manifest can remain the source, but digitising it does not remove the need to understand the load and check actual goods.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct loading depends on actual packages, vehicle constraints and delivery sequence.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital manifests provide information without replacing physical checking or handling.
tasks.still_hard: Missing goods, awkward loads and differences between list and stock.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when the listed load cannot be carried as planned.
tasks.altitude: No change to manifest understanding or loading duties.

reach.task: Resolve missing or conflicting goods before departure
reach.learn: Which load discrepancies require a revised manifest

evidence.claim: The design retains manifest understanding and physical loading without claiming digital-document runtime as a new saving.

assumptions: Boundary is reviewing issued drops and loading, excluding creating the dispatch plan and driving.
The existing dispatcher produces the drop list through unchanged planning; s1 counts the worker's interpretation and goods checks.
No structured package discrepancy or automated load-suitability flag is assumed; s2 retains physical handling and discrepancy detection.
No new system or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Load types, existing manifests and loading constraints
research_questions: Is there actual duplicate manifest entry outside necessary review and physical loading?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+75=100. List review and physical loading retain their full time with zero incremental upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce standard order drafting while retaining customer contact and physical route work.
reach: Give sales managers clear nonstandard requests and dispatchers clear load discrepancies
role.ambitious_version: Complete route sales with clear standard records and accountable customer commitments.
